utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-08-91-T. The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, before I ask for the appearances, the record would note that the Bench is fully constituted with the return of Judge Harhoff. Thank you, may I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. For the Prosecution I'm Tom Hannis appearing with our Case Manager, Crispian Smith. And I had requested a chance to address one brief procedural issue before the witness came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic for Stojan Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just wanted to bring one matter to your attention. I'm not requesting any specific relief at this point because I'm not sure I'll need it. But this morning I received an e-mail listing I think some 94 documents that the Defence proposed to use in cross-examination, and it's my understanding that these were ones that had not been previously notified as being possible -- possibly used with him. That may not cause me any difficulty. I see of the 94 some 80 are 65 ter, therefore, documents that were on the Prosecution's list, so it's something I should have some vague familiarity with. But it's been four weeks plus since we last were with Mr. Nielsen, so it bothers me that I only got notice of this morning instead of last week or two weeks ago. That's all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Is there any comment from the other side?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, most of the documents which are provided in the list to Mr. Hannis are already exhibits in the case. Therefore, we didn't feel that this would cause any prejudice or problem for the -- for our learned friends from the Prosecution side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I note you said "most."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would say 95 per cent are the exhibits already in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We'll see where we go. The Chamber has before it the Prosecution's third motion for leave to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit list to add documents relating to the present witness, and the substance of the motion is that this deals with a document which the Prosecution could not have earlier confirmed that it would be using. The Defence, I assume, having had recent notice of this - this motion was filed the 22nd of January which is Friday past - the question is how much time does the Defence need in order to deal with this new document. If either side is in a position to indicate that now, it would be useful. But the -- let me not volunteer any more. Let me hear what the Defence has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I would first like to let the record show that Mr. O'Sullivan has joined us in Stanisic Defence. Concerning this document, we are ready to proceed. We received the document on Friday, and I informed my learned friend that the Stanisic Defence would have no objection to it, and we can proceed with this document. But there is one other aspect. This document which we are talking about is a response to a letter sent by Mr. Karadzic. And I have asked Mr. Hannis in order to have a complete set of these documents which refer to a fairly contested issue in this case, that maybe it would be better if all of these documents which are in possession or which the Office of the Prosecutor is in a position to obtain, that all of these documents are provided to the parties and then we can -- then we can, I believe, completely deal with this issue. That was the gist of my suggestion to Mr. Hannis. And concerning this particular document, we are fine, we can proceed, and we don't require any additional time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. And no doubt we would hear further from Mr. Hannis on your discussion. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage we don't have any particular objections, but please give me additional time that during the break I have to check with my team the exact details of these documents. But this principle I think that everything would be fine with Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That's understandable, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I do apologise, Your Honours. If we are speaking about Mr. Hannis, we are speaking about these two documents, correspondence between the Cutileiro office, and that's all. Only these two documents. One. I don't have objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, the point that Mr. Zecevic made about the documents in respect of which the subject document was a response to, perhaps you shouldn't be put on the spot of answering formally now, but we would require response after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will check. I know we made an inquiry as to whether or not I had a letter to which the present one I'm asking to be admitted is a response to, the 12 June letter from Cutileiro to Mr. Karadzic. And I have asked one of my assistants to check and see if we have the letter to from Mr. Karadzic that prompted this response and I certainly agree if we have, we should include that as well, and I'll try and report to you after the break if we do have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that disposes of all the preliminary matters. Could the marshal escort the witness back to the stand, please. I keep saying marshal, I should use the word "usher." I forget I am not where I used to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Your cross-examination continues, welcome back and we wish you all the best for the new year. Before I invite counsel for Stanisic to continue, the Chamber would remind you that according to our calculations, you have an hour and a half left with the cross-examination of Dr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours, I believe there was -- there was a discussion before we adjourned last year and we were of -- our understanding was rather that the Trial Chamber would grant us the whole day of proceedings for ... I'm now suggested by my co-counsel and counsel for Zupljanin Defence that actually the decision has been taken in that respect. That, if you remember, we requested additional time, and there was a discussion about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I confess that I'm relying largely on my own recollection which may not be accurate. Aided, of course, by such records as the Registry has. But does counsel for the Prosecution share Mr. Zecevic's recollection of this ruling the Chamber made?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm checking the transcript now, Your Honour. I recall there was a discussion about it. I don't recall the outcome, frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can be of assistance, Your Honour. Honourable Judge Delvoie was presiding at that day, and we have detailed discussion about the timing, and finally, the decision was made that Stanisic Defence will have one day; Zupljanin, one day; and Prosecution for redirect, one day. That's the ruling that I know that it was somewhere at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Which will account for the three days that we have assigned for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We thank counsel, and the transcript now confirms what Mr. Pantelic has indicated. So that Mr. Zecevic has one day, Mr. Pantelic has one day, and the Prosecution has one day. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, may I begin with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to hand a small binder to our expert witness Mr. Nielsen containing the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Obviously we have to continue. If you will remember last time we left off at the point of commenting on certain laws that are crucial for understanding the place and the role and the jurisdiction of the Ministry of the Interior. However, what we left out and in your work and your report starting from paragraph 175, you are dealing with the internal regulations of the Ministry of the Interior for the adoption of which Mr. Stanisic was bound to do that according to all the internal regulations and the law. Is that correct? I apologise, we don't have Mr. Nielsen's answer on the record, to my previous question. Mr. Nielsen, can you please repeat your answer to my previous question, it hasn't been recorded.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Again we don't have it on the record, please repeat, I don't know if you can see the record.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. We may proceed now. These internal regulations were to be adopted as an obligation by Mr. Stanisic based on the Law on State Administration and the Law on the Interior in order to govern the internal relations within the ministry of the interior and its organs that were not governed by the law or more precisely regulated, although they were provided in the law because you would agree with me it is not possible to include everything in a law; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In these paragraphs to which I referred, beginning with number 75, you justly -- I am sorry, Mr. Nielsen's answers keep not being recorded. The problem must be that you understand me and you hastened to answer, so we overlap. Could you please answer again my previous question.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, and, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In the quoted paragraphs you already dealt with one of these documents. First and foremost, the rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior under the circumstances of immediate threat of war and the state of war; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I say you justly dealt with it because that is, in fact, the most important and the most extensive internal document for whose adoption the minister was responsible; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly was the most extensive internal document, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And physically, it is indeed very voluminous, it weighs several kilos. And with that document the minister practically stipulates the internal organisation of the ministry beginning from the minister at the top down to the clerk and employee who performs the simplest jobs such as janitors, cleaners, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, although it should be noted that despite its voluminous size, it was about half as long as the previous SRBiH rule book on the same subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. In that document what is enumerated are the job descriptions of every employee that required training and qualifications, the way of contracting employment, termination of employment, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] That is the point of the document; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In that binder, the first document is number 20. I apologise, we need on record your previous answer.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is the point of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In that small binder I've given you under number 20, you will find the record from the extended session of the collegium of the MUP dated 9th September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the Trial Chamber it's Exhibit 65 ter 239.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: While the Registrar is looking for the document you can see that the agenda featured the consideration of the draft document on internal organisation under number 2.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thus you will agree in the month of September it had already been prepared in the form of a draft, as they called it, but it had not been passed yet?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I state that in paragraph 176 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe you stated that at one of the collegium sessions in November, the minister insisted that it should be urgently adopted. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Nielsen, at this time from September to November was a time when this document, according to the procedure, had to be forwarded to every employee in the remotest police station, and every employee had the right to put forward his suggestions and comments. Are you familiar with this procedure of adoption of such documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that all leading employees of the MUP, for example, chiefs of public security stations and Security Services Centres were invited to comment upon the draft document. I have to admit that I wasn't aware that every single employee of the ministry was invited to comment upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me tell you then this time from September to November passed precisely in collecting these comments and suggestions and during Mr. Stanisic's tenure, the document was not adopted among other reasons because of the announced resignation of Mr. Djeric which was taken November, do you know about this problem in the functioning of the Government of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. Mr. Djeric resigned from his position at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree, though, that this area did not remain uncovered because the organisation operated all the time based on the old book of rules of the Ministry of the Interior, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I believe you mentioned it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and just as we mentioned last year with the law, the new rule book is in large part based on the previously existing rule book.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Correct, I agree with you. To conclude with these rules, I'd just ask you to look at a set of documents that the minister adopted in this period, and they were indeed enacted there in the binder. Let me just go through them briefly, not in detail, we don't have time for that. For instance, the rules on discipline and disciplinary liability of the employees of the Ministry of the Interior. It's under 20.1. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's already an exhibit, so I won't call it up on the screen. Let me just ask you, did you have occasion to look at it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and, in fact, I can see based on the ERN that this was one of the documents that I personally collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you had occasion to evaluate --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, let me tell the Trial Chamber that it's 1D54 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you had occasion to evaluate that the minister simplified and abbreviated the procedure for establishing disciplinary liability and extended the statute of limitations for disciplinary infractions to double the length? Have you noticed that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that as with the rule book on the internal organisation of the ministry, the regulations on disciplinary responsibility were made more effective or stream-lined, we could say. However, I've not studied in detail the statute of limitations for disciplinary infractions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, then we won't deal with it in detail. Could I ask you to look at another document from this set. It's 20.10. And it's 65 ter 1860.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the legal officer can help us get this document on the screen. It's a report, a progress report for July, September 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We won't discuss this report much. It will probably be recalled when we discuss other topics. Let us just turn to the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me find it first. It's page 19. That's the page number, and that's how we can probably find it in e-court. In B/C/S it's 19. No, this is 16. We have to turn three pages further. We need page 19. Right, that's the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we find the right page in English. I have to be honest, I have not prepared the references in English, but my colleagues tell me it's number 25 -- 24 in English, page 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We just opened this page, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we scroll down a little in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We find a short list on this page and on the next page, a list of documents that the minister passed in the course of his tenure up to September 1992. That's the end date of the report. There are nine rules, five draft laws were suggested in this period because the minister sometimes even proposes bills in its own jurisdiction and a number of orders and instructions, et cetera. My question regarding all these documents in the binder including instructions that have been exhibited such as the instruction on compulsory current reporting, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I notice that there's a slight difference between the B/C/S version and the English version which are on the screen of the documents. It appears that the Serbian version actually does mention five draft laws, but the English version only contains four. I don't know if this is of any significance, but maybe we can just clear it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask my colleague who speaks English to assist me. It seems the only one missing is the third law, the law amending the law on the personal identification card. The third line in the list from Serbian is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Nielsen, this includes also all the major instructions. 1D51, which we will not open. In your set it's 20.6, instructions on current interim and other reporting, as well as a number of other instructions. And in your work you dealt with these instructions and a series of orders that the ministry used to control the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I would note that this is a document from September -- excuse me, October 1992, and that means that as is indicated at the beginning of the section, not all of these administrative and draft law proposals have yet been adopted, but they have all been drafted and are intended to be adopted for the use of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as draft laws are concerned, but you will agree with me that in this period, and that's the point of my last question here, the minister endorsed all the necessary internal documents for the operation of the Ministry of the Interior except these last rules that were not adopted during his tenure?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the end of that topic, and you won't need the binder anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to hand to you the next binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Among those internal documents the minister passed, there is about -- there are about ten orders that have been a subject of your study and also the Prosecution. In your evidence and in your paper --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction of the transcript. It's not about ten orders, it's about several dozen orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You dealt in greater detail with one particular order; namely, the order to establish a staff for the contingency of war. You dealt with that in direct examination. But before we open the document, may I ask you to look at the document number 1 in the binder. It's 1D00-4042, but I won't open it. I'll instead say what it is. I quoted from this law several times, and I will just ask you to follow. It's the Law on All People's Defence; correct? Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If you don't mind, open to Article 91. Right. I will read and you just confirm whether I read correctly, because you do speak my language. "The armed forces constitute" --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't speak the language. Could we have a reference to where it is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then we have to open Article 91 in English. We opened it with the previous witness. This will take a lot of time. Can we find Article 91 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English it's 61; right? We have both versions now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's enough to read it out; I don't have to interpret it. It's defined here what the armed forces are. They consist of the Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now just move to Article 104, page 67 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: One question applies to all three articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in Serbian it's page 18, Article 104. If we could just zoom in on that article.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In your report you do mention the principle of resubordination. "In situations of immediate threat of war and other contingencies, the police may also be used to carry out combat tasks of the armed forces in keeping with the law. During its engagement for combat activities in the armed forces, the police shall be under the command of the authorised officer in charge of the combat activity." That is written in the law. I think I found a passage about this in your report, do you agree with this principle?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, and I'm familiar with that principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And there's another article, 207.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we find the corresponding pages. That's correct. We have it in B/C/S. Let's just see where it is in English. Page 115 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, according to military regulations in the system of All People's Defence, all subjects in the state are duty-bound to prepare for All People's Defence, to make plans, to form staffs, and take all the other necessary steps for the purpose of defence preparations and continued work under the circumstances of immediate threat of war and war. That's what this article is about. I don't know if you had occasion to study it, but you must be familiar with the general principle from studying the system of All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that, and in the report I note that the president of the RS government, Branko Djeric, issued instructions for all institutions in the RS to draft such operating guide-lines in accordance with the relevant regulations. I don't think I referred to that article but that was surely the point of his instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Now we can move on to 65 ter 126. That's Exhibit 1D46.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you are familiar with this order. I think you have commented on it in your previous testimony. So, Mr. Nielsen, this obligation to draw up plans in the event of an imminent threat of war or a state of war is an obligation that applies to the Ministry of the Interior as well as it does to all other state organs, this is what you have just said when you mentioned Mr. Djeric.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is an obligation that applies to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You commented on this order until item 7 inclusive. Can we now please look at item 8, and can we just briefly comment on it. Have you found item number 8? Let's see if we have it on our screens. I think that's the case. It reads literally as follows: "In carrying out regular duties and tasks, the provisions of the law on internal affairs and other regulations of the Serbian Republic of BH currently in force shall be strictly upheld." This is what the minister says in this order. And then it goes on to say: "Whereas in military operations military regulations and rules shall be enforced." My question relating to item 8 is be very short. Isn't it true, Mr. Nielsen, that this item 8 provides for the pure application of the rules and regulation that we were discussing previously? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is the point of this item 8 with respect to the engagement of police personnel in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I agree with your comment, and I would have to move now to next document, that's number 1 in your binder, which is Exhibit 1D00-3610. We have to wait for it to appear in e-court. Mr. Nielsen, as you may have noticed, from the heading this is an enactment issued by the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina whereby both the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska as well is dealing with the issue of wartime organisation. Do you agree? I apologise, I meant Bosnia-Herzegovina. And that in this document, if you look at page 5 -- can you please have page 5 of this document. Please look at paragraphs 1 and 2. Minister Alija Delimustafic expresses his dissatisfaction with the flaws established in the course of preparation of public security stations. And in paragraph 2, the lack of analysis of the work and functioning of these stations within the system of wartime organisation. Can you see that? What is evident from this is that the joint Ministry of the Interior was obliged to draw up these plans and also to draw up the wartime organisational chart of the joint Ministry of the Interior, this is what stems from this document, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated earlier, most of the relevant regulations enacted in the Republika Srpska were either copies of or slightly revised versions of the relevant regulations in SRBiH MUP; therefore, it is entirely correct that this is the point of this document, and I'm also aware that Minister Delimustafic as well as other leading officials of the old SRBiH MUP were highly unsatisfied with the situation on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, because we believe that this is a relevant document, I tender it to be admitted into evidence because it is linked to the order that we had previously discussed. This is 1D00-3610.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't object to the admission of this document, but I need some clarification about this statement, how Delimustafic's document is related to the previous document by Minister Stanisic on the 15th of May 1992? Is that what is being said? I don't see how Minister Stanisic in May 1992 is creating war units based on something that Delimustafic said in March 1992 before there was a break in the joint MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the point is that they are both operating on the basis of the same regulations and drawing up the wartime internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior. What I want to say is that what Mr. Stanisic did was nothing that he made up himself that has a foundation in the previous practice that went on for years. So if you want to delay the admission of this document once you have seen the next one, I think the things will become more clear. Both Mr. Stanisic's order and this document and the next one have a foundation in one and the same regulation, and this is where I see the connection between those; and for that reason I'm tendering it to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D158, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I apologise, I've been criticised by my learned friend Zecevic. I've been criticised for not following the sequence of documents. Can we please now have document 1D00-0454.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in your binder, Mr. Nielsen, that's number -- actually, that is the document before this one. 1D00-0454, you found it, and I think we also have it on our screens. The essence is that in the document that's just been admitted was preceded by a 1991 document addressed to all the administrations of the joint Ministry of the Interior. And can you please focus on last paragraph on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please scroll up. That's right. And I don't know whether the corresponding paragraph in English is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I think in paragraph 3 it says that there is an obligation to prepare a proposal for assigning employees, and for that purpose I'm providing the necessary forms, a list of employees assigned to MUP according to the wartime organisation including all the jobs in your organisation under the rules in force, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we please look at the attachment to this document. It's a form. And I think it's page 3 in both versions. Yes, that's the relevant form. Can we please have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, have you found this form? What we have here is a list of employees assigned to the SUP according to the -- MUP, according to the wartime organisation. I see that number 1 is minister of the interior, then his deputy Vitomir Zepinic, et cetera, et cetera. So you would agree with me that this confirms what we discussed previously, i.e., that this wartime organisation and the operation of the MUP, so to speak, functioned on the basis of the same principles and the same rules and regulations; am I right, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the document we are currently looking at reflects the fact that the leading officials of SRBiH MUP, because of a severely deteriorating security situation to which we have previously referred, drafted the necessary preparations or contingency plans for the operation of the ministry should a state of war be declared. And certainly in RS MUP, Minister Stanisic, again although there was not an official state of war declared, set up the ministry to function as if war conditions obtained.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I think that we agreed on one thing, that was essentially only the application in both cases of the Law on All People's Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have wrapped up this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I suggest that this document be admitted into evidence as Defence exhibit. Its number is 1D00-0454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D159, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, the next document in your binder is number 6, and I'm trying to find it in your report, this particular area that you dealt with. This is an area concerning camps, collection centres, and points where people were detained in 1992. That's the subject that you have dedicated a whole chapter to. Let me just find the beginning, and maybe you can help me to do it as quickly as possible. Yes, that's paragraph 285 until the end of the next chapter. Have you found it? Shall I wait for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit 2079 according to 65 ter on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree, Mr. Nielsen, at least according to the number in the binder, that this is an extremely complex and extensive area. We cannot discuss it in detail, and we cannot discuss all the documents. In line with the Chamber's guide-lines, I have made selections of the documents and divided them into groups, and I will tell you which group I'm particularly referring to. This is a decision on the application of international humanitarian law [as interpreted]. Mr. Nielsen, have you found --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: International Laws of War.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you found this order on the implementation of International Laws of Wars, you can see that this order was issued by the president. It's dated the 13th of May, 1992. Let us look at item 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we have the right document. That's not item 3 that I was referring to. Please move to the next page. Item 3 on the next page in B/C/S. The English version is okay. Let's look at item 3 in the B/C/S. It's up there in the upper part. Which reads "the minister is authorised." Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: According to the president's order: "The Minister of Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is authorised to prepare instructions on the treatment of captured persons." I'm showing you this for the sole purpose of identifying it as an initial regulation which indicates that the problem of the application of the international laws of war with regard to the treatment of captives has been identified by the state leadership and that the president and the Presidency have assumed their role according to the constitution and law to address this issue in a proper way. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree that Radovan Karadzic in his capacity as president of the Presidency issued this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: {Interpretation] I don't know whether this has been admitted into evidence. If not, I tender this short order, or rather, short regulation to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, isn't this part of what we've been referring to as the law library?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I withdraw my proposal. I agree with the Chamber. Let's move on to Exhibit P189, which is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That's document 6.1 in your binder. Mr. Nielsen, in order to implement this order an instruction on the treatment of captured persons were issued, and it was signed by Mr. Subotic, the defence minister. Attached to this instruction was a sort of card or a form to be filled out for each captured person. Had you had an opportunity to see this instruction?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this order and these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are now going to deal with a series of orders and instructions of President Karadzic, records of the meetings of the Presidency. I will go through them quickly because they all refer to the same subject, and probably inviting we shall submit to the Chamber a list of all the exhibits that need to be admitted into evidence. I just want the witness to confirm whether he had opportunity to read that or not. Can we please look at document 65 ter 186.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's 612 [as interpreted] in your binder, Mr. Nielsen. I see you have already found it. You can see here that Mr. Karadzic continues to be seized of that problem. He makes reference to the international law and, therefore, issues instructions how to treat the civilian population in case they become detained. We are not going to comment on it. Can we simply just read it to ourselves. And then we have the next document which is another order issued by Mr. Karadzic. Let me just say that this was repeated on the 19th of October. That's 65 ter 222. Let me see, that's 6.3 in your binder and you have it, as I can see. Practically in this order Mr. Karadzic emphasises an obligation to adhere to international covenants. The same was done by him on the 6th of August, 1992, which is document 6.5 in your binder, and it's already in evidence as P191. He also appointed certain persons in charge of various issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since it's already in evidence we need not look at it. And we have one more document from October. It's actually dated 22nd October. That's 65 ter 259.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in your binder, it's 6.4, Mr. Nielsen. Yes. Mr. Nielsen, at least as far as Mr. Karadzic's document are concerned, we have learned what the position of President Karadzic was regarding this issue. He addressed this issue by issuing orders and conclusions with regard to the application of international Laws of War. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, it's 10.25. Is this a convenient point?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you say so, Your Honours, I would agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment and resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted back to the stand, I need to return to something that occurred on Friday in terms of the -- an order for redaction that was made. And it turns out that there is a portion of the transcript which indeed not have been redacted, so, therefore, the order that is now being made is that in terms of Friday's transcript, page 80 line 20 to page 83 line 10, the time code being 1324 to 1330 hours, that need not have been redacted, is, therefore, restored to the public record of Friday's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, during the break, I was informed by Mr. Zupljanin that he has certain problems with his neck, due to previous long time ago accident, so he would kindly ask if he can get to use one of these chairs with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If it's available, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, now we come to a series of records from the sessions of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'll just read out the number of the exhibits, we don't need to open them. P201, P427.18, and 1D104. It's 66, 67, and 68 for you. You can confirm to the Trial Chamber that these are records from the 23rd, 24th, and 25th session of the Presidency of Republika Srpska. Let's just look at the dates. 5th June and 8th August 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you just confirm that in the record of the 23rd session of the 5th of June in the agenda, item 2, it says that the issue of prisoners of war was considered, as well as the issue of their accommodation and food for them. Was that issue really discussed, can you confirm?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm that the next session also discussed this topic, and so did the 25th session. It says a particular issue was the one of camps and security. That's your document 6.8, page 1, the penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the Presidency dealt with this issue continuously, especially in the month of August. Do you agree that it was on the agenda on all the three sessions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I note that the reason that that was the case, the reason why the Presidency was so interested in that subject, as I note in my report, was the fact that the conditions in detention facilities had become an international issue at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Before I move to the next topic, I have to ask you to go back to P189. We don't need to open it. These are the instructions by General Subotic. Item 18 is the one we need to look at because it has to do with my next question. For you is number 6.1. For the organisation and the accommodation in camps, corps commanders of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are responsible. That's what General Subotic assigned to them as their obligation. Do you agree? Item 18 in the instructions.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is what points 18 says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up P61.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: For you, Mr. Nielsen, it's number 7. I just want to look at the establishment of military camps. As you can see, obviously in keeping with the prior decisions of the Presidency, General Ratko Mladic also issued a document called the treatment of prisoners of war. And in this document he mainly interprets the documents of the Supreme Command referring to international treaties, providing a basis for the establishment of military camps for prisoners of war. Have you had occasion to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's already exhibited so we can move on to the next one. Your number 8. 1D156. In the series of these orders by General Mladic, there is one that we are going to see in a second. Take your time if you have not seen it before. On page 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the legal officer. We need page 2 immediately. Paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It says, the corps establishes a camp for prisoners of war. Number 8, have you found it? Now move to page 2. Paragraph 3 begins with the words that, "the corps shall establish a camp for prisoners of war in keeping with our order," et cetera. Mladic orders the Eastern Bosnia corps to establish a POW camp in the spirit of the general order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, the English on the screen doesn't appear to be matching up with what is being discussed. At least on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's point 2 in the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see it now. Is it all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, Ratko Mladic now implements his own order ordering a specific camp to be set up; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to another document. Let me see if it's exhibited. 1D157.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your number 9. Now we have the order of the commander of the Eastern Bosnia Corps setting up a POW camp on the Batkovic farm and like in the order by General Mladic, the conditions under which the camp will operate are determined, the way security is provided, et cetera. Mr. Nielsen, you know that the Batkovic camp was a military camp; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that Batkovic was a military camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then I will show you documents for a couple of other military camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P427.14.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's your number 10. It's from the command of the Birac Brigade. Look at point 6 where the commander, Major Svetozar Andric deals with the evacuation of the Muslim population, what it should look like, what do with men, women, and children, and this is addressed to the staff of the Territorial Defence of the Zvornik municipality. Do you know that on the territory of the Zvornik municipality, one camp was established on the basis of this order?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree that that is what the document says in point 6. I'm familiar, as I noted, with Batkovic, but I'm not familiar with the specific existence of military detention facilities in Zvornik municipality since I, in my report, mostly focus on detention facilities operated by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up 65 ter 1463. It's a decision of the commanding officer in whose area of responsibility it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In item 1 you can see that a camp was organised in Vlasenica, and the name should be familiar to you, Susica camp. Were you aware that this was a military camp?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar from other cases at this Tribunal that Susica was a military detention facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since this is not yet an exhibit, may I tender it now. I believe it's relevant and the witness is familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure the witness said he was familiar with the document, but I don't have any objection to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D160, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to proceed more quickly. Let's move to document 65 ter 1457. Your number 12. We need item 8 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is a daily operation report from the command of the Eastern Bosnia Corps which notes that in the area of Zvornik there are around 500 prisoners in the area of Zvornik and another 800 in the area of Vlasenica. I'm just trying to show how the need to form POW camps arose. The numbers grew and the units were no longer able to take charge of them so camps needed to be set up. I suppose that you are not familiar with the document, but this document demonstrates the need to form -- to set up POW camps, and I would like to tender it. I am sorry, I didn't ask my question. Do you agree with my position that it is reports like this that show the need to set up such camps because operational units cannot take responsibility for prisoners and conduct combat activities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that documents like this indicate one reason and one way in which detention facilities were formed on the territory of Republika Srpska, in this case by the military. I have to say that I'm not previously familiar with this document which was collected; I can see based on the ERN after I left the Tribunal. But I would like to note since we do have this document in front of us that point 3 of this document actually speaks to the police and says that there is often shooting in villages and in the city without any reason for that, and the police does not intend to prevent this, so that obviously relates to my subject of analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, but my question was about the need to set up POW camps. You can agree that this document precedes the establishment of such a camp, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D161, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 642 will be our next document. In item 4 we see an identical situation. It's again a combat report, but now we are in the sector of the 1st Krajina Corps, and in item 4 the same is noted, that they have 600 prisoners of war and they are facing the same problem. This document confirms the same point as the document we exhibited, so I tender this document as well, 65 ter 642.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D162, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to show you a document that has been exhibited, P61.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, if I may go back Mr. Cvijetic. Although in terms of the sequence of documents, as I understand it, I acceded to the application that it be admitted and given an exhibit number, was there a question to the witness in respect of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document was identical to the previous one, so my questions on the previous document apply to this one as well. I can only repeat the same question, does point 4 confirm the need to set up POW camps, because operational units cannot guard them. It's the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand that, but perhaps for completeness, the witness should be invited to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You heard the question, Witness. Would your answer be the same as to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, again with my caveat that this is not the only reason why detention facilities are being formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe we already have the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What are, then, the other reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in my expert opinion, I believe that the use of the term "prisoners of war" in this and the previous document in practice, when analysed in the context of all available documentation, shows that the term "prisoners of war" was, in fact, applied in a blanket manner to a lot of persons in municipalities controlled by the RS who had at no point been engaged in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you are saying that these camps ended up holding not only POWs, but also civilians. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and that is reflected in both the military and the police documentation that I have been able to examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, this order from the command of the 1st Krajina Corps is probably something you have seen before. Measures of reinforced security are applied here, or are to be applied pursuant to this order, and the command and the Chief of Staff specify these reinforced measures and the use of civilian police as guards. P61.1. Have you found that? Pursuant, therefore, to an order from the military command, the civilian police is engaged to provide security in a facility like this. Would you agree that at the moment when they take up such a duty in the area of responsibility of a military unit, a civilian -- the civilian police place themselves under the command of that military unit in executing their security tasks?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, and I would point out, as I do in the report, that the minister of Internal Affairs and other leading officials of the ministry on several occasions objected to the use of police officials to guard military detention facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I agree on that point. I will then not dwell long on the next document. 65 ter 3026. Your number 15. Here we have a study on the Susica camp prepared by the warden concerning the guard service. And he, like the command of the 1st Krajina Corps -- let me just find the page. Page 6. Page 6 contains a table. The legal officer pulled it up for us. He envisages military men to provide security and the civilian police is engaged only for reinforced security. It's obviously the same system as in Manjaca, the military always followed the same principles, and it's the military commander here who decides how security will be provided. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not been able to read the entire document through, but based on the parts that you have shown to me, that is what it appears to indicate. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tender this, 65 ter 3026.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D163, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document will be your number 16, Exhibit 1D03-0496. I don't know if it's in e-court. Has it been translated? I apologise, we have to take a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's finish with the military with this document. It's from the administration for intelligence and security affairs of the Main Staff. President Karadzic decided on the 25th December to disband the Manjaca camp as a sign of goodwill and to reduce the tensions among the international public, et cetera. Do you agree that a decision like this could not be carried out that easily, not even if it carried the authority of the Main Staff and the Supreme Command, because it says here by disbanding the camp they would be letting go even of the most hardened criminals and those responsible for the gravest crimes. So this provides for a selective approach to the execution of an order from the Supreme Command. Do agree that it was not impossible to ensure uniform conduct in this case, not even pursuant to the order of the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, with the greatest respect, although Mr. Nielsen is an expert witness, I'm not sure that the way that question was phrased which seemed to incorporate more submissions and argument than anything else, is one that he could helpfully answer. Perhaps you may wish to rephrase it as a more focused question. In any event, the document speaks for itself. Any conclusions to be drawn from it would be a matter for submissions at the appropriate stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. I forgot an introductory question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you had occasion to see a document like this before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this and similar documents and would note what is an interesting point, namely, that despite the fact that many of these people have been in detention for a period of weeks, or even months, it is still the case at the end of 1992 that criminal complaints have not been filed against many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The point of my question was this, and you can agree or disagree, does this look like resistance to the decision of the Supreme Command in a sense?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it looks like disobedience. It looks as comments from the field which are designed to alert the president to the fact that the status, legal status of a number of detained persons has still not been determined, specifically again because they have, for whatever reason, not raised criminal complaints against many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously there's no more discussion possible on this document. I will not tender it, Your Honours. Can we move to the next document, 65 ter 1396.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As you can see, it's a decision, your number 17. A decision to establish penitentiary and re-education facilities in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina adopted by the Presidency. I just want us to identify another type of facility where people were detained. These are official penitentiary institutions in Republika Srpska where certain regulations applied. And you will agree with me they were within the jurisdiction of the justice ministry of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct; that is what this document discusses.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D164, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next document, 1D00-2309.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's Doboj. Can you just open your own document from the set. It's just one page, next page. Page 3. This is the affirmation of the translator in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need in B/C/S a page which corresponds to the current English one. In B/C/S it's 2. Page 2 in B/C/S and page 3 in English. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we've now read a decision to establish penitentiary correctional facilities, but here we see an interesting document from the district prison in Doboj, you've read it. From this we see that a report on the situation in that prison is sent to the Crisis Staff of Doboj municipality. I believe you dealt with this topic, the influence of the Crisis Staffs, even on affairs of this. How do you explain that? There is the proper organisation, there is the justice ministry, and yet we see that Crisis Staffs deal also with penitentiary institutions.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note that this document stems from the end of June 1992. From the large quantity of documentation that I've been able to examine, it is certainly the case that in the first three months, particularly in the first three months of the RS's existence, the Crisis Staffs engaged themselves proactively and extensively in all manners of activities in municipalities in the RS. I note that, in fact, my section in the report on RS MUP and the operation of detention facilities in the RS notes that the police themselves formed the Omarska facility pursuant to an order of -- or a decision of the Prijedor Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document, 1D00-2309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D165, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll move on now to the next two documents. One of them is P193 already in evidence. It's your number 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with this exhibit. Let us just see how the document dealt with this issue. They adopted a decision on former commission for business to collective centre. You have reviewed it, so there's no need for us to comment on it. Let's us just see how the government addressed this issue. You have seen this document, can you please confirm that for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if it's already in evidence and he is not going to ask the witness to comment on it, I don't know why we need to show it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have asked him to confirm whether he has reviewed this document or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The next one is P194. I assume that you are familiar with the results of the work of this commission. I would just like to draw your attention to page 6, that is the last page of this document. Specifically item 4 where it is suggested that all these facilities should be handed over for security to the Army of Republika Srpska. Are you familiar with this document and these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document. I believe that I discuss it and analyse it in my report, and I would note that the point in number 4 is completely consistent with my findings, namely that as of August 1992, not least because of the international outrage regarding detention facilities in the RS, the Ministry of Internal Affairs was very actively and very rapidly trying to divest itself of any involvement in the operation of such facilities. In some cases --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move to the next topic, if you don't mind. I think we dealt with this document sufficiently. Mr. Nielsen, you have just mentioned the decisions of the Crisis Staff. Let me just check whether you had this document in mind, which is document 21 in your binder, and that is actually 1D00-0183. You speak about the setting up of Omarska camp on the basis of a Crisis Staff decision, and I think you also had the same camp in mind in your footnote; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is the document I referred to. This is merely a different version which doesn't have the same ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document to be admitted into evidence because the witness is familiar with it, and he makes reference to it in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D166, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have now document 65 ter 443, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We are still dealing with Crisis Staff decisions. Here we have a decision adopted by the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality on the release of people from detention. You will agree with me that this matches your point, and that is that the Crisis Staff were very much involved in the issue of prisoners, even on deciding who was going to be released from detention camps or not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I want to note that these Crisis Staffs, of course, as a matter of routine included at the municipal level the chief of the public security station as a representative of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D167, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the next is 65 ter 472.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: It's an order from the same Crisis Staff. Your number 23. It's an order to all enterprises and agencies to terminate the employment of workers who had participated in the armed rebellion, armed insurgency, and who are currently in Omarska and Keraterm. The decision to up to the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document says; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Have you had opportunity to see a document like this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D168, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next 65 ter 1880. Your number 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: These are minutes of the session of the National Defence Council of the Prijedor municipality, dated 29th September, 1992. And please look at sub-items 1, 2, and 3 under item 1 -- item 2, sorry. So item 2, there are sub-items 1, 2, and 3. You can see what decisions this council made. It takes over all the essential obligations regarding the unhindered arrival -- sorry departure of all persons from the open Trnopolje reception centre, the public security station is to provide escort for the convoy; and subitem 3, the municipal Red Cross is advised to close down the open Trnopolje reception centre. So at the municipal level major decisions are made regarding these centres in Prijedor. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that significant decisions are made. And I would again point out that Simo Drljaca who was the chief of the public security station in the municipality of Prijedor is a member of the Crisis Staff and is a member of the body that is making these decisions. So these decisions are made with police participation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D169, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nielsen, I'm going to finish with number of documents of Mr. Mico Stanisic, and for that purpose can we have Exhibit D55. It's your number 33, I apologise. So 1D55.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, have you seen this order issued by Mr. Mico Stanisic before? In this document, Mr. Stanisic is dealing with how detention measures should be applied. And in item 2 it says a security collection centre shall be directly -- will be the direct responsibility of the Serbian army. And if they do not have enough men for this duty, it shall therefore be necessary to engage members of the reserve police for the task and to place them at the army's disposition. You mentioned this issue and I would like to remind you of the law on the Internal Affairs, the Criminal Code. Within public security stations, there were rooms in which people could be detained for up to three days. The subject of this order is particularly those premises, those rooms; is that right? The minister hereby determines what kind of conditions regarding hygiene should exist. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've asked me several questions, so I'll start with the first one. And that is that I'm not previously not familiar with this document. I can only assume that it is among those documents which the OTP was unable to collect and which Mr. Stanisic discussed during his interview with the OTP. In response to your second question, this document is indeed consistent with the other documentation that I have been able to analyse in the sense that we know that already at the mid-July 1992 meeting of the leadership of RS MUP in Belgrade, concern was expressed about deplorable, un-hygenic, unsanitary, and dissatisfactory conditions in detention facilities. So in that sense, this seems to be a logical effort by Mr. Stanisic to remedy that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, Mr. Stanisic here speaks about detention units within public security stations in which the police is entitled to detain persons for up to three days.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel please speak more slowly and repeat his last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic -- Mr. Nielsen, hold on a minute. The interpreters simply did not get the question that was asked by counsel. So for the record, Mr. Cvijetic, would you be good enough to repeat your question. And again I remind you not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, this order obviously refers to remand prison units within the police premises in which the police can detain people for up to three days. As for all other facilities, it deals under item 2 specifying that the police is not responsible and it's not its jurisdiction to deal with these matters. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would agree with that conclusion with the observation, however, that this order is issued on the 10th of August, 1992, a point at which the police is still involved in operating large-scale detention facilities that were being shut down in the course of August and September of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that I don't agree with what you said last, I'm going to move to the next document which is already in evidence, which is 1D56. Will you please read this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I ask if counsel does not intend to tender that last one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's already exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been admitted before, Mr. Hannis. Just like the one that we see right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, my position and the Defence position is identical in this regard, and that is to say that Mr. Stanisic is dealing solely with these affairs only within his remit. As for other detention and collection centres, he clearly states that it goes beyond his jurisdiction. Is that an inference that can be drawn from his orders?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact of the matter is that at the 11 July 1992 meeting in Belgrade, the minister and all other leading officials of the ministry clearly, as is revealed in the record of that meeting, discussed unsanitary and deplorable conditions in detention facilities, and the need to remedy that situation. That is why in examining this document, which I do in my report, I put it in the context of a general effort by the minister to ameliorate the situation in detention facilities in the RS; to clearly indicate who is responsible for what facilities, to -- as for his ambitions to remove the police eventually from the business of guarding and operating detention facilities; and finally to investigate and close down, as he says in this order in front of us, any wild, I'm not sure what the best English translation would be, wild prisons which might exist on the territory of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, the last document that I'm going to show you, let me just check the number. It's already in evidence, and it's 1D57. 1D57. You can see this document. It's your number 37. It's a document forwarded by the minister to the centres and public security stations by making reference to the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and with a view to collecting information about detention and collection centre in the territory of Republika Srpska. The minister says regardless of jurisdiction, it is necessary that you provide the following data, and underneath he lists what specific information he requires. I'm not going to show you proof that this order actually reached all the centres and the stations because I don't have time for that. My question is the same as before, it is obvious that Mr. Stanisic distinguishes between these camps and detention facilities, but he is not trying to avoid helping other organs in providing this information. One of the ways of doing that is by sending this circular letter. Do you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again let me say clearly that the documentation shows that both the army of the RS as well as the MUP of the RS operated detention facilities in the summer of 1992. As of August 1992, as I indicated in my previous answer, the RS MUP was proactively trying to divest itself as quickly as possible of any involvement with detention facilities. The order in front of you -- or the document in front of us, I agree, shows that the minister in accordance with orders issued by the Presidency at that point wants to clarify the exact situation on the entire territory of the RS according to existing prisons, detention facilities, and camps, regardless of who is at that point in time operating those.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, at the end I will state the Defence position, and I will give you an opportunity to either agree with it or not. The Ministry of the Interior under the Law of Criminal Procedure and the enactments adopted by the MUP, and the Law on Criminal Procedure and Internal Affairs has the right to detain persons for whom there is reasonable suspicion that they have committed criminal offences for up to three days. To that end, they have the right and the capability to have certain premises for these purposes in their stations. All Mr. Stanisic's orders refer exclusively to these cells and premises. As for all other facilities, camps, collection centres, call them what you will, the Ministry of the Interior has no jurisdiction over. There is not a single order issued by the MUP minister in which he ordered or supported or encouraged the establishment of any such facility of this other kind. There is no order in which the minister ordered the use of members of the police in providing security of such facilities.
