On the contrary, all his efforts were aimed at excluding the police from any security related affairs concerning these facilities, and that these facilities be handed over to the army. Mr. Nielsen, do you agree with what I have already said whether that was within the system or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That's a very compound question. It's argumentative, and it assumes facts not in evidence. He needs to break it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I note that it runs from line 53 through to line -- sorry, line 5 to line 25. It's almost a speech, Mr. Cvijetic. Again, could you attempt to phrase the question in a manner that the witness can give an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, have you in your examination found any order issued by Mr. Stanisic according to which he ordered the establishment of camps or detention centres that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not found any orders issued by Mr. Stanisic in which he personally orders the establishment of such facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever found any order issued by Mr. Mico Stanisic in which he orders or gives an instruction to use members of the police to provide security in such facilities, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer would be, yes, I have found orders issued by Mr. Mico Stanisic in which he certainly treats the use of members of the police to provide security in such facilities, and indicates awareness that such engagement was ongoing. However, in all of those documents, he also seems to indicate, particularly after the 11 July 1992 meeting, his position that the police should as quickly as possible hand such responsibilities over to the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I insist on my question. Have you ever found an order whereby he issues an order or an instruction to use the police for those purposes?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, with this I conclude my cross-examination, and I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, before you leave this witness, I would like to just have your last point clarified a bit because I think that earlier on you did offer evidence to the Court that police officers could be resubordinated to the army in times of an imminent threat to war or in wartimes. And so it would appear that, in fact, police officers could in some instances be resubordinated to the army to assist in operations that were related to the war. That is to say, not only taking part in an armed operation, but also to assist in other activities associated with such an operation, for instance, the running of a camp. So I just want to be sure how these two pieces of evidence relate to each other. Because on the one hand it seems as if actually police officers could be resubordinated to such tasks as guarding or ensuring the security of camps, and on the other hand you maintain that Mr. Stanisic never issued any such orders. How are we to reconcile these two pieces of evidence? Can you clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We had a previous witness when you were absent. He was a professional military man. It was a protected witness so I am not going to name him. He had worked in one of these camps, and he gave very definitive answers to this question. I believe the other judges remember. There is no dilemma in the minds of the military in this respect. The minister of the interior does not decide on questions like the engagement of the police in combat activities and in the security service of camps. It is the corps commander and the warden of the camp who take these decisions. These orders were not even notified to the minister, at least in the aspect that we discussed. That's how I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So your point is that the MUP and the minister of the interior had no influence over the use of military personnel in the running of the camps except, of course, the camps that fell under the direct authority of MUP. Is that your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is our position, our case, that no camp was under the direct control of the Ministry of the Interior under the law. And from the evidence that we presented today, this does not follow. As for the use of policemen to provide security at military facilities, we have made this perfectly clear, including with the evidence led so far that it was done pursuant to the orders of military commanders beginning with General Mladic to corps commander. And under the circumstances of immediate threat of war and such circumstances, the ministry had to comply, especially in the area of responsibility of a military unit. And this professional officer told us that in that area of responsibility, nobody can discuss the order of the military commander. It has to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. But my point was -- and please help me to clarify if I have misunderstood. My point was that detention facilities for ordinary civilian crime, completely unrelated to the war efforts, that such camps were in fact coming under the authority of the Ministry of the Interior; is that correct? So I have misunderstood, then please clarify. Who was in charge of the running of an ordinary detention facility for civilian crime?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are penitentiary correctional facilities. Official institutions under the law. And it is the Ministry of Justice that has jurisdiction over them. That is not a fact in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, it's time for the break, so you may wish to resume when we return.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. I was just wondering if we will make the switch like in hockey, so thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nielsen, on your right you will see two binders. Please pick them up to facilitate and to speed up our discussion of certain documents because my time is limited. The topic I want to discuss is in chapter 4 of your expert report titled, "The MUP of Republika Srpska and the War in Bosnia-Herzegovina." To sum up, in paragraph 191 you state the position that I completely disagree with and consider inaccurate; namely, and I'll para-phrase, The MUP of Republika Srpska played the main part in the war and was the only military power until the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska which was exclusively and directly controlled by the leadership of Republika Srpska, and it was considered a part of the armed forces. Did I para-phrase your position correctly?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, really you're para-phrasing the position of Mrs. Plavsic, which I was para-phrasing, but, yes, that's the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose since it's in your paragraph 191 that you adopted that position as your own?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I include that statement or a similar statement, as you noted, in the report, because I believe that it accurately reflects the statements of the RS leadership at the time concerning the composition of the armed forces and the role of the RS MUP during the early phase of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, my colleague put to you Articles 91 and 104 of the law from which it is quite clear that the only two branches of the armed forces are the army and the Territorial Defence, not the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would point to the fact that Radovan Karadzic in his capacity as president of the RS, when he issued an order or decision on the formation of the high command of the RS armed forces, included the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the definition of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, would you please focus and answer my questions. We will come to your arguments related to the Supreme Command at some later point, but you said yourself that the Supreme Command was set up only towards the end of 1992. I'm asking you if it is true, if it is correct that my colleague put to you articles of the law on All People's Defence, Articles 91 and 104 which say explicitly that the armed forces are made up of the army and the Territorial Defence, not the police; do you remember that? You confirmed that not so long ago.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the specific articles, I agree that that reflects the de jure situation. However, the de facto situation is that the RS leadership and the officials of the MUP through an extensive part of this period referred to the MUP as part of the armed force and that Biljana Plavsic referred to RS MUP specifically as "Nasa Vojska," our army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I understand your need to add, but we are now wasting time needlessly. My question was, if it was the situation under the law, and if I understood correctly, you confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, asked and answered. He did confirm that de jure that was the situation. And this problem started by Mr. Zecevic para-phasing what was in Mr. Nielsen's report. If he would have quoted directly from the report, we wouldn't have this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. I was trying to deal the best I can with the issue of my limited time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, let's look at the de facto situation you are referring to. Look at P183. It's number 1 for you. It's a decision of the 15th of April, that the lady you mentioned, Mrs. Biljana Plavsic and Dr. Nikola Koljevic, members of the Presidency of Republika Srpska adopted to proclaim the immediate threat of war and mobilisation. Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see in point 2 it says that mobilisation of the Territorial Defence in the whole territory of Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina is thereby ordered and all conscripts have the duty to make themselves available to municipal Territorial Defence staffs in their areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the next document, 1D03-0491. It's a document of the Ministry of Defence, 16 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that your answer has not been recorded in the transcript. I think he confirmed that point 2 indeed contains what I read out, but I can ask him again. Would you please repeat your answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document we are looking at now, your tab 2, is the decision to set up the Territorial Defence as an armed force of the Serbian Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it goes on to explain who will lead it. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this before? It's signed by the Defence minister, Bogdan Subotic.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it before as it's cited in other expert reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, can I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D170, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The next document is 1D00-2721. The decision on the general and public mobilisation and requisition of assets in the republic passed by the president of the Presidency on the 20th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here in point 2, all military conscripts are ordered to report immediately to the nearest units and commands of the army, and then we see the date of commencement of the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there's no objection, I move to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D171, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Nielsen, to the best of your knowledge, and from your studies and research, isn't it the case that the Territorial Defence was organised into units along military principles?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding of how the Territorial Defence functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: They had commanders and ranks and all the other aspects of military organisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because pursuant to the prevalent military doctrine at the time, the Territorial Defence was complementary to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As part of the armed forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In times of war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This military doctrine you refer to, does not mention the police, does it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does to the extent that you, yourself, quoted from the relevant defence legislation which states that the police can be resubordinated to the military during times of conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I fully agree with that, but apart from that, it is not claimed that the police is part of the armed forces. The doctrine states that the Territorial Defence and the army are the only ones that make up the armed forces in wartime; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can I have a reference to what document counsel is referring to as stating the military document -- or the "military doctrine"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not stating a specific document. The document I stated is a part of the military doctrine which is the Law on All People's Defence. The witness himself said that the prevalent military doctrine at the time considered the Territorial Defence as complementary to the JNA. And that is the basis of my question. I wasn't referring to any specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind as to answer my question, Mr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you, and that's precisely the interesting innovation that the RS makes in the course of 1992, namely to include the police in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "innovation" you are basing that on these statements by certain politicians and the fact of setting up the Supreme Command; right? Those are the main two elements?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are two of the elements. They are not the only elements; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You must know that in these initial stages of the conflict, April, May, and June 1992, so-called light partisan brigades were formed in certain municipalities.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly know that light brigades were formed in certain municipalities. Whether or not they were called partisan, I have to admit I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you worked in the Office of the Prosecutor for a long time and you are a Prosecution expert, you certainly know that in the Stakic and Brdjanin judgements, the Trial Chambers found that those light partisan brigades that had been set up in certain places initially had been outside the structure of the Army of Republika Srpska and outside of the commands. That is one of the facts offered for stipulation in this case as well. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the finding was that they were outside the structure of the Army of Republika Srpska, or that they were outside the structure of the JNA, but I'll have to take your word for it at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to one of the elements on which you base the conclusion that the police was indeed included in the armed forces, allegedly, namely this decision on the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska, 65 ter 271. It's your number 4. You now have the document before you. It's a document to establish the Supreme Command of the Army of Republika Srpska signed by President Karadzic on the 30th of November 1992, and you quoted -- you cite it as one of the elements supporting your position; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose you have read this decision because you reference it in one of your footnotes?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read every decision that I reference in a footnote, so, yes, that assumption is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I thought. When you were reading, didn't you notice in Article 1 the reasons why the so-called Supreme Command of the VRS was established? It says for the purpose of harmonisation and co-ordinating and improving the sufficiency of the command system of the VRS. Did you make note of that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As always, we think in similar ways, and yes, I did notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As you said a moment ago under the military doctrine prevalent at the time, Territorial Defence would also be complementary to the army. And under that doctrine it would fall under the command of the army in circumstances of immediate threat of war or war?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Article 5 also states: "Final decisions by the Supreme Command of the Army of Republika Srpska on the basis of the constitution and the law are the responsibility of the president of Republika Srpska." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, that is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which means that this Supreme Command is a consulting body for harmonisation and co-ordination, whereas decisions are definitively made by the president of the republic in the interests of the country and its defence, as the law stipulates; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Article 5 says that the president's decision is final and that is, of course, reflected in orders given to both the MUP and the VRS to coordinate better throughout 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is the case, isn't it, that you cited this document in your report as a proof of innovation, as you call it, namely the inclusion of the police in the armed forces, only because of Article 3 -- sorry, Article 2, which says that, "the Supreme Command of the VRS consists of," and then enumerates various elements ending with the minister of the interior. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, that is but one of the elements that led me to that observation which I make in the report. It's based in large part also on the characterisation by the RS MUP in its own reports of its own relationship to the VRS and its own role as part of the armed forces in what they saw as the struggle for the liberation of the Serbian nation. It's also based, as I note in paragraph 381 of my report, on the fact that RS MUP engaged to a massive extent over 300.000 man days monthly in participation on average in combat activities by the forces of RS MUP together with the VRS in joint operations. So it's a large number of documents and an overall analytical observation that I make here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we are now discussing this particular element. We discussed quite sufficiently the possibility of resubordinating the police to the VRS on the basis of other documents, now I'm asking you about this document. Since you answered in the affirmative that it was one of the reasons why you cited this, I'm asking you if you noticed Article 4 in this decision which states that the Supreme Command may include other ministers and other authorities in its work?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that article of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it the case, Mr. Nielsen, that Djeric's government practically fell, or rather resigned on the 24th November 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Djeric actually resigned, I believe, at the end of October, but that it took effect, I think, around that date that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And all the ministers from that moment until the end of December and January next year operated as a technical government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is the case, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you, yourself, said it was the de facto situation, did you look at what happened at these sessions of the Supreme Command in order to establish what the de facto situation was?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not had the opportunity to review those sessions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you restricted yourself to this decision, and you haven't looked at a single session of the Supreme Command; is that what you are trying to say?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to say that the ambit of my report was such that I was aware that the relevant military documentation, the details of what was going on at that Supreme Command, were being looked at by the military expert; so, no, you are correct in saying that I have not looked at the sessions of the Supreme Command from the end of November 1992 until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know, but sir, since you express this as your position about the de facto situation, I only assume that it would be logical for you in order to establish whether that was actually the de facto situation or not, you should have looked at how this decision that you have taken as one of the element operated in practice; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my position that the document that was issued, this decision which was issued by President Karadzic on the 30th of November 1992, in fact, reflects quite accurately the de facto situation up until that date. Now, as to what happened after that date and if it -- if it in any way contradicted the spirit or the letter of this document, I'm certainly willing to examine any documents that you might want to show to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, maybe my English is not good enough, is it your evidence that this decision of the 30th of November had a retroactive effect? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not what I'm saying. I would differentiate in any case between orders that have an explicit retroactive effect, and there are examples of such orders being issued in 1992 by various institutions, and orders that do not have an explicit retroactive effect but confirm an existing de facto situation. Those to my analytical mind are two different things, and what I'm saying is that this order in many respects confirms an existing de facto situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, what you are trying to say is that the Supreme Command of Republika Srpska existed before the 30th of November 1992; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is again misconstruing what I just said. What I'm saying is that there are an enormous amount of examples for ongoing co-ordination on practical, technical, and legal matters between military and police organs going back to the formation of the VRS in May 1992, and that, as such, this institutionalisation of such consultation and co-ordination is a logical culmination of a de facto situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, with all due respect, I under that you are an analysis, but you have to base your analysis on facts and not on arbitrary constructions; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm basing my analysis on facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm very glad to hear that. We are just now examining these facts, but I seem to misunderstand things. Let us now move on to document --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before that, I would tender document 271 according to 65 ter into evidence, which is a decision to establish Supreme Command of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D172, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please look at document 1936, according to 65 ter. That was the only session of the Supreme Command that took place in 1992, i.e., on the 22nd of December of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I'm looking at this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So for the benefit of the Chamber, I'm going to tell you that on page 2 in paragraph -- or rather, paragraph 4, I believe, V. Lukic is mentioned here as a prime minister elect which means that he already attended this session of the Supreme Command. And on page 3 in the penultimate paragraph, we see an address delivered by Mr. Stanisic, that is on page 3 in e-court in both versions. Mr. Nielsen, although I believe you haven't read the entire document since you probably might find it difficult to comment on it, but I'm going to say that at this session of the Supreme Command, Mr. Stanisic and I would like that to use as administration of what the Supreme Command actually was. Minister Stanisic says that a situation related to Golf vehicles should be investigated. He speaks about the formation of para groups. He is talking about the reinforcement of military judiciary. And he says that there was no co-ordination between the military and civilian police forces. That was the role of the interior minister as member of the Supreme Command. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that conforms to the kind of co-ordination activities to which I previously referred.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I thought you wanted to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say co-ordinated activities, isn't it true that in combatting crime, the minister of the interior insisted on the fact that criminal offences were being committed by members of the army. However, because of legal regulations, the members of the police didn't have any authority or jurisdiction over them? That is to say, to undertake measures that should be taken under the law against such perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am aware that that is one of the matters that was discussed between the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the army. I think not to hang it up on a semantic point, but I'm talking both about co-ordinated activities, "koordinirane activnosti," and activities of co-ordination, "activnosti koordinacija," which are subtly different things, but a forum in which two institutions which are central to the functioning of the state have a plenum in which they can discuss the issues that involve both of their ministries and forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Nielsen. Would you allow for a possibility that in your report with regard to the position of the MUP as part of the armed forces, you have committed an error?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think part of the problem we've been having here is that I think counsel seems to be using "armed forces," in quotations marks, as maybe that term as described in a particular law, as opposed to armed forces in generic sense as a force carrying arms and engaging in combat. If we could have some clarification for his question to the witness, that may resolve some of the wrangling that we have been having.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with the suggestion of my learned friend, given that in the introduction I think I have clarified with the witness, Mr. Nielsen, here that I'm referring to the armed forces as defined by the law, whereby they are made up by the army and the Territorial Defence and not the police. So whenever I make a reference to the armed forces, this is what I mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I clarify, that's the 1982 law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's the law on All People's Defence adopted in the Law on National Defence of Republika Srpska in February 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, can you answer my question. Do you think that it is possible that you have committed an error?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you specify what error you are accusing me of having committed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That you have included members of the Ministry of the Interior among the armed forces who both under the law and de facto were not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the sense that that is a mistake, then it is a mistake that's not only made by myself, but in fact by the RS leadership at the time, who repeatedly refer to the -- again in a de facto sense, as the RS MUP as a critical part of the armed forces of the RS and as a critical element in achieving the military and strategic objectives of the RS, as they do throughout 1982. But in a de jure sense, if it's the very narrow point of whether it's a mistake on the de jure sense, then I -- and with narrow reference to the 1982 law, then I absolutely accept your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear that. Just one more comment. You are an intellectual, you have a PhD, you are an analyst, and I cannot accept that you -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this doesn't sound like a question. He indicated, I have one more comment, and now he is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just laying foundation for the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the words uttered by politicians cannot carry the same weight as documents and legal norms. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In what context? Could we have some clarification. That's a vague question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness said that he had based his conclusions on the words uttered by the RS leadership, that is to say on the speeches delivered by politicians on certain public occasions. I put to him the documents and the laws. I'm just asking him whether he puts these two sources at the same level regarding the weight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So phrased the witness may answer the question, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My answer is that I think that I would neither as a professor nor as an analyst be doing mu job properly if I were only to examine the de jure situation during a period in which it is abundantly clear that it was in fact the de facto situation that was more often obtaining in the field. And I would again note that the RS MUP which itself, including its very top leadership, was itself made up of lawyers, that they themselves were guilty of committing this conflation consistently throughout 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to comment on politician's competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at 1D36004 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would use that to point out to you a difference between the legal concept that existed in Republika Srpska and the one that existed in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can page 3 be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, this is a decision adopted by the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 4th of April 1992. It provides for mobilisation to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's the Presidency -- adopted by the Presidency on the 4th of April 1992, which pursuant to the decision of the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina the mobilisation of the Territorial Defence units shall be carried out in all municipalities and towns in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Have you seen this document? I think it is your tab number 6.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 3 of this document reads that the entire reserve force of police in Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be carried out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I tender this document into evidence if there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection. And may I inquire if he intended to tender the previous 65 ter, 1936?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thought it wasn't fair to the witness to tender this document. I am interested in doing so, but since the witness hadn't seen it before, I don't think it's fair to tender it through this witness. For the most part, I made comments and I put to the witness specific parts and for that reason I didn't tender it into evidence. There will definitely be another witness through whom we can tender this document, but if Mr. Hannis insists on this and if he has no objection, I would like to tender it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't insist, I have no objection, though I have no doubt that it's authentic, and I think it's relevant, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It may be neater -- I take Mr. Zecevic's reservations about the tenuous connection between the witness and that previous document, but it may be neater to tender it now. So the documents are sequentially admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D173 and Exhibit 1D174, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to be completely clear, 1936 is 1D173, and 1D36004 shall become 1D174; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now in sequence the following document, 1D00-4381. It was signed by the then defence minister of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It carries the same date which is the 5th of April 1992. It was signed by Mr. Jerko Doko, and this document actually constitutes an elaboration of the previous conclusion adopted by the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Mr. Nielsen, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that I have, and I note that it doesn't have an ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm surprised that you haven't seen it. It's a public document. Very briefly I will lead you through it. This document refers to the Presidency document ordering general mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and the reserve police. This is a very important document that can help explain what you and I discussed a moment ago. On page 2 of this document, the Defence minister, Mr. Jerko Doko entrusted the ministry of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina to secure, if necessary, appropriate weapons and assets for units of the Territorial Defence. That's on page 2 under the heading of "Conclusions." Last line under item 2. And item 3, that's on the next page, reads ... that's the first sentence on page 3 of this document. It reads that units of the Territorial Defence that are mobilised for carrying out the above-listed task under the quoted regulation shall be subordinated to the public security and will act in compliance with the orders of the officers of the Ministry of the Interior. The commanding officers of these units should be informed about this. With regard to command and control of the mobilised TO units, the TO staffs must also strictly respect the fact that the units are subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Mr. Nielsen, I am surprised that you haven't reviewed this document either before or while you were writing your report. What stems from this is that in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in April 1992 -- I see that Mr. Hannis is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interject. Your Honour, we don't have an ERN. I don't know if this is -- I don't know the source of this document. I see it appears to be a telegram. It's not signed. I have some vague recollection in the back of my mind that Mr. Doko either when he testified or when he was interviewed about this denied that this document came from him. So I have some questions about the validity. I may be mistaking the document, but I believe there was one, and I bring it to your attention, and I will be objecting the admission of this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not aware of Mr. Doko making any objection to this document. We received it from the centre for research of war crimes of Republika Srpska. And on page 1 it has the stamp of the municipal Territorial Defence staff in Visegrad, which leads us to conclude that this document that was issued in Sarajevo by the minister was truly and actually received by the TO staff in Visegrad. On that basis, I concluded that this is an authentic document and that it was delivered to all TO staffs as indicated in the heading of the document itself. But as far as I'm concerned, we may mark this document for identification. And once we have cleared up the situation, we may then tender it to the Trial Chamber for admitting into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That was going to be my suggestion, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I hope that Mr. Hannis agrees for this document to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. That will give me time to research my questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Are you asking it to be so marked at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 1D175, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Nielsen, it stems from this document, that in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina the Territorial Defence was resubordinated to the Ministry of the Interior. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think it's important to note here that this is taking place at a very, very late date. This is already the 5th of April, 1992, when the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is practically ceasing to exist. And they are obviously, in the same document that we have in front of us, taking issue with what they view as the illegal formation of RS MUP and other activities in the republic. So it's a very particular situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think that for the purposes of this case, this represents one of the early documents because it's dated the 5th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm speaking of the context of the life span, if you will, of the SRBiH which was certainly on its last legs as of the 5th of April 1992, not this the context of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, my impression is in light of my previous comment regarding your report, is that you have made a mistake. When you commented these documents of the SRBiH where it is obvious that the Ministry of the Interior and its members were part of the armed forces of the republic, when you compared the de facto and de jure situation Republika Srpska in which members of the Ministry of the Interior were not members of the armed forces, and when you say armed forces, again I'm repeating that I have in mind the legal formulation from the Law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Law on National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in that context, I asked you whether this situation was the reason for you to draw an erroneous conclusion in your report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a point of logic, I find it hard to see how I could reach an allegedly wrong conclusion based on a document which I've told you I have never seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In many places you've reached a number of conclusions based on the de facto situation, so I thought perhaps in this case, too, you meant the de facto situation?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not referring to this de facto situation, which in any case, I clearly see and I think we can all clearly see, refers not to what is going on in the nascent Republika Srpska but rather in the SRBiH which is soon to re-emerge as the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Just one more question on this. Do you believe that this document I've just shown you that was MFI'd, do you believe it to be relevant to your report or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that assuming that it's authentic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Assuming that it's authentic, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With that caveat, I don't really think so, in the sense that the ambit of my report is to treat SRBiH MUP, and then once SRBiH MUP ceases to exist, RS MUP. This document is taking -- is being written in the context after RS MUP has been formed, and I obviously do not, in my report, engage in any analysis of what the, if you will, Rump Bosnian MUP looked like, interesting though that may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You mean the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina when you say this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina which continued to exist and to operate as the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina and as the successor to SRBiH MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move to another topic. Deportation and forced transfers. In your report, paragraphs 320 to 329 -- and again because of time limitations, I'll have to para-phrase your general position because if I read all the nine paragraphs, it would last too long. Generally, it is your position that the police of Republika Srpska was involved in deportations and forcible transfers of the population; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the police of Republika Srpska at some times and in some locations did take part in such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood your report correctly, you base that finding on a couple of facts that you interpret in your own way. One, insufficient security for all the citizens especially Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the way in which the RS MUP describes the security situation, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And second, the fact that a significant number of non-Serbs were leaving the territories of areas affected by the war and combat?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, as you call it, fact is reflected also in RS MUP reports; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And, three, another fact that you use to support your finding are the so-called operations of cleansing or mopping up of the territory?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do note that the RS MUP was involved in mopping-up activities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And finally, your fourth element is the involvement of police officers in disarming operations. You place that in the context of forced transfers and deportation.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not the final element, but yes, that is another element of the analysis; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'll take these four elements because I thought them the most important for this topic. To take them in order, the second point was the fact that a significant number of non-Serbs were leaving territories affected by the war in combat. Do you know that at one point President Karadzic issued an order forbidding the departure of people from the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that he issued an order forbidding the departure of males of military age from the Republika Srpska. I am not aware off the top of my head with the general order forbidding the departure of all people from the territory of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, that will be enough. Do you know the conclusions of the London conference on the free movement of civilians in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as I stated previously, I'm not an expert on international conferences on the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you as an expert, I'm asking you about the facts. Are you saying that you are unaware of the fact that there was an agreement between the parties to the conflict dated 22nd May 1992, that had been signed with the assistance of the ICRC on the 22nd of May in Geneva, on the free movement of civilians and some other matters?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that specific fact, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just show the witness 1D00-3943.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document, and maybe it will jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I remind you, you have five minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then show the witness P427.23.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's another document from the same series, agreement number 2, dated 23rd May, also relating to exchanges of prisoners, lifting the siege from various features and deblocking civilian population, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I have not seen that document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is in the nature of things that if there was an agreement between the parties, that means that both Serbs and non-Serbs evacuated from certain territories and resettled in others; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that involves quite a bit of wishful thinking, but I'm not excluding that such matters were discussed and even perhaps agreed to in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you certainly know, I suppose, that a large number of Serbs had been expelled from certain territories in Bosnia-Herzegovina and moved to the territory of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was -- there were very large movements of Serbs from certain territories, as you call them, in Bosnia-Herzegovina to the territory under the control of the RS. And I'm also aware, of course, of similarly large movements of Bosniaks and Croats during the same time-period in the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Don't you think that these facts have a certain impact on the movement of persons from one territory to another, a matter that you discussed in your expert report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly it is the case, and it's reflected in the documents that I quote, that there were large movements of people with concurrent deleterious consequences for the security situation, and that is reflected in the RS MUP documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, just one more document. P160. It's a document of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska from July 1992. It's a summary of the meeting that was held on the 19th of July. You have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I quote it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to turn to page 20 to see the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court -- just a moment. I can see the clock, Your Honours. As you know, as you see, I have not completed because our assessment was not very good. I know I don't have the moral right to ask for another extension, but I believe that these matters are very serious, and it would assist the Trial Chamber to clarify them. We have done what we could. I discussed it with the Defence team of Mr. Zupljanin, and they are prepared to give me one hour from their time allocation tomorrow that I could use to finish my cross-examination with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, in as much as the witness is here for three days, if Mr. Pantelic is so generous as to afford you a portion of his time, I don't suppose there's any harm, but we'll have to see what happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We'll have to finish the cross-examination by Mr. Zecevic tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Allowing Mr. Hannis his Wednesday, whatever arrangement as is arrived at between counsel for Zupljanin and Stanisic would be all right as far as the Chamber is concerned. But I don't know that Mr. Hannis would be a part of these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Well, Your Honours, if the situation arises, we will talk to Mr. Hannis as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's what I just want to say. We count on Mr. Hannis in these negotiations, if we would need some more time, I hope that he will generously give something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to say if it has no impact on me having the full day on Wednesday, I don't know care if Mr. Zecevic goes all day tomorrow and Mr. Pantelic only has one minute. Frankly, much of the time, I'd rather hear Mr. Zecevic than Mr. Pantelic anyway. But you take my point, but I don't care how they divide the time among themselves, but I generally oppose any extension of the time beyond Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Anyway, we'll take the adjournment now until tomorrow. According to this schedule, we are in this Courtroom mornings for the remainder of the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And one matter before you go, Your Honour. Regarding the Prosecution's pending motion to add that document for this witness, I have confirmed that the letter that Mr. Zecevic wanted us to include was already included in the earlier motion as 65 ter 3463, that being a letter of 5 June from Dr. Karadzic to Mr. Cutileiro.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I can concur, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of January, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
